deficiencies.description: The rewrite introduces an unsourced causal link using 'because', claiming that benign tumours are extremely common because it takes a great deal for them to become malignant. The lecturer merely made two separate statements.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: So benign tumors are actually incredibly common. Right? So it actually takes a lot for a benign tumor to become malignant in terms of, as I said, the number of changes that have to happen within a tumor. So they're extremely common
deficiencies.rewritePassage: Benign tumours are extremely common, because it takes a great deal for a benign tumour to become malignant, given the number of changes that have to happen within a tumour.

considerations.reason: Omitting 'for example' in 'Malignant tumours originating from mesenchymal lineage cell types are extremely rare' does not distort the factual claim about mesenchymal tumours.

considerations.sourcePassage: So I've just put these numbers up just so that you can have a sense.
considerations.reason: Phrasing this as 'The numbers shown give a sense of incidence' is contextually faithful to the topic of incidence being discussed.
